lesson.title: The Pusher: Change the Game
lesson.hook: They get everything back, so you hit harder, and they get that back too.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you play a pusher, change the game by the fourth ball instead of the fortieth.

pro.label: The drop in Nadal's comeback
pro.moment: Two sets down to Medvedev, famous for standing deep, Nadal used the drop shot to drag him forward. Medvedev tried drop shots too, against a Nadal who stood closer in. Nadal won 63% of his drop-shot points. Medvedev won 46%.
pro.read: Same shot, same match, opposite results. Where they stood decided it.

stroke.title: drive vs drop
cues: Up to here they look identical. That's the disguise: they can't read it early.
The drive drops below the ball and brushes up. The drop stays above it and slides under, so the ball floats with backspin.
No follow-through over the shoulder. Slow the racquet, don't stop it.
stroke.pro: Alcaraz adds a second disguise: he often drops it the opposite way to where they're split-stepping. Hugh Clarke, analysis

drill.name: The deep-or-up game
drill.how: Your partner loops from 2 m behind their baseline. Any ball that lands inside your service line, you must drop it. Driving it back loses the point. After 5 points they move up to the baseline, and now only a deep approach counts. First to 7.

lesson.cue: Deep? Drop it. Up? Come in.

steps.name: Ten balls, same loop
steps.sit: They're 2 m behind their baseline, looping everything back. This one lands short enough to step in on.
steps.q: How do you break the pattern?
opts: Hit it harder, to the corner
Same crosscourt, wait for an error
steps.payoff: They live deep. Your drop made them sprint 12 m, and they couldn't get there.
steps.principle: Pushers are comfortable at the back. Bring them forward.
steps.why: From that deep, pace just comes back: they have time. A drop from inside the court lands where they aren't, and they run out of time.
steps.take: Pusher deep? Step in and drop it short, away from them.

lines.A: Harder, but from 2 m back they have time — it comes back.
lines.B: From inside the court, angled away — they can't get there.
lines.C: Deep and safe — the same rally, their way.
lines.D: Same ball, same rally — they won't miss first.

steps.name: They got to your drop
steps.sit: This time they reach your drop and pop it up. Now they're stuck on the net, 2 m away.
steps.payoff: They were too close to the net to cover the lob.
steps.principle: Once they're forward, go over them.
steps.why: On top of the net they can volley anything at chest height, and a drop just sits up for them. A topspin lob goes over, and they can't turn in time.
steps.take: Pusher pulled to the net? Topspin lob over them.

lines.A: Right onto their racquet — volleyed away.
lines.B: At the net, they get across — volleyed away.
lines.C: Slow and short, and they're right there — they put it away.
lines.D: Over them — they can't turn and run it down.

steps.name: They move up
steps.sit: They've learned: now they stand right on their baseline. The same short loop comes to you.
opts: Hit it harder, to the corner
steps.payoff: They wouldn't stay back, so you came forward and finished at the net.
steps.principle: If they won't come forward, you do.
steps.why: Standing on the baseline they run the drop down and pass you. Their passes are soft, so a deep approach and closing in wins the point.
steps.take: Pusher on the baseline? Approach deep and finish at the net.

lines.A: Deep approach, you close in — their soft pass, put away.
lines.B: They're closer now — they run it down and pass you.
lines.C: Same rally — they won't miss first.
lines.D: Harder, and it still comes back.
